name: United Kingdom
description: Britain from Stonehenge and Roman rule through Saxons, Normans, Tudors and the Industrial Revolution to empire, world wars and Brexit.

checkpoints.name: Stone and Rome
checkpoints.note: Farmers raise Stonehenge, Celtic tribes build hill forts, and Rome rules Britain for nearly four centuries and builds Hadrian's Wall.

checkpoints.name: Anglo-Saxons and Vikings
checkpoints.note: Angles and Saxons settle England, and Vikings raid and then settle the north and east. Alfred the Great holds Wessex, and his heirs unite England.

checkpoints.name: Normans and Plantagenets
checkpoints.note: William of Normandy conquers England in 1066. Plantagenet kings rule from England to Aquitaine, Magna Carta is sealed and the first Parliaments meet.

checkpoints.name: Lancaster, York and the Tudors
checkpoints.note: The Wars of the Roses end with Henry Tudor. Henry VIII breaks with Rome, and Elizabeth I sees off the Spanish Armada in the age of Shakespeare.

checkpoints.name: Stuarts and union
checkpoints.note: One king rules England and Scotland. Civil war ends with a king beheaded, the Glorious Revolution sets Parliament above the crown, and the two kingdoms unite in 1707.

checkpoints.name: Industry and empire
checkpoints.note: Under the Hanoverian kings Britain leads the Industrial Revolution and builds the largest empire in history. Queen Victoria reigns for 63 years.

checkpoints.name: The Windsors and two world wars
checkpoints.note: Britain fights and wins two world wars at great cost, Ireland leaves the union and Churchill leads the country through its darkest hour.

checkpoints.name: A new Britain
checkpoints.note: The empire ends and the NHS begins. Elizabeth II reigns for seventy years, Britain joins Europe and then leaves it, and Charles III becomes king.
